summary: Inside the elevator, Neo — uneasy about the idea of learning his fate — questions Morpheus about the Oracle. Morpheus confirms she is the same one who made the prophecy, that she is very old, has been with them since the beginning of the Resistance, and knows enough rather than everything. Neo presses whether she is never wrong; Morpheus reframes it, calling her a guide who can help Neo find the path. When Neo asks if she helped Morpheus, Morpheus says yes and reveals she told him he would find the One. The elevator dings and opens.

what_changes.before: Uncertain about the Oracle's nature and reliability, asking if she knows everything.
what_changes.after: Learns the Oracle is a fallible-sounding guide who 'knows enough' and cannot be judged in terms of right and wrong.
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: Don't think of it in terms

what_changes.before: Guiding Neo in the abstract, describing the Oracle generally.
what_changes.after: Discloses that the Oracle personally told him he would find the One, grounding his faith in her in his own destiny.
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: That I would find the One.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus prepares Neo for meeting the Oracle by explaining who she is and what she told him.

uncertain: Exactly what unease Neo feels about learning his fate, beyond that it 'begins to weigh upon him'.
Whether Trinity or others are present in the elevator (only Neo and Morpheus are shown and speak).

minds.wants: To pin down, before he commits to seeing her, whether the Oracle is reliable — specifically whether she is infallible — so he can judge what she will tell him about his own fate.
minds.feels: A steadily growing unease at the prospect of learning what is predestined for him; the 'uh', the rapid-fire follow-ups ('The beginning?', 'Everything?', 'And she's never wrong'), and the pivot to asking about Morpheus's own experience are all the anxiety of someone being led toward a verdict about himself and trying to test the authority of the person who will deliver it.
minds.shows: Only curiosity and a slightly nervous, probing interrogation — a man asking reasonable questions about a mysterious figure. He keeps the fear of what the answer might be for him off his face.
minds.basis: The narration states 'The idea of learning one's [.].' His questions escalate in a way that tracks that unease (prophecy → beginning → everything → never wrong), and he redirects from the abstract to Morpheus's personal case ('She helped you? What did she tell you?') rather than answering the fear directly.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus speaks from certainty and can be relied on as a guide to the truth about the Oracle.
That Morpheus's faith is founded on something testable — that asking 'what did she tell you?' will reveal a measurable basis for his confidence.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus's certainty rests on faith, not on a fulfilled test: the Oracle only told him he *would* find the One, which is precisely what cannot be verified until Neo either is or is not that One. Neo is asking for proof and being handed a prophecy.

minds.wants: To prepare Neo to meet the Oracle without letting Neo's doubt about her infallibility turn into doubt about the prophecy itself — steering him from 'is she right or wrong?' to 'she is a guide.'
minds.feels: Absolute, quietly held conviction. He is not describing a fortune-teller; he is describing the source of his own life's meaning, and the revelation that she told him he would find the One is the emotional peak of the exchange, offered deliberately as the ground he stands on.
minds.shows: Calm, economical, almost cryptic authority — he answers in riddles ('She would say she knows enough,' 'Don't categorize your thoughts using moral absolutes.') and only at the end, when pressed, personalizes it. He lets the certainty show through the mystery rather than explaining it away.
minds.basis: He reframes Neo's 'never wrong' into 'guide' ('Don't worry about right or wrong. She's your guide, Neo. She'll show you the way.'), a move that protects the prophecy from being falsified by a simple right/wrong test. He then answers 'Yes' to 'She helped you?' and delivers 'That I would find the One' — grounding his entire faith in a personal, unfulfilled prediction.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is the One he was told he would find — that the Oracle's word to him is now being fulfilled in this young man.
That Neo can be led to faith the way he himself was — through trust in the guide rather than through proof.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is the opposite temperament: he keeps demanding verification ('Everything?', 'never wrong') and, as later events show, will need to see the Oracle's answer for himself rather than accept it on Morpheus's authority.

connects_back: sc-079: Neo already framed the Oracle as the one who can tell you 'who you are,' and Trinity's inability to speak when asked what the Oracle told her plants the seed of both mystery and danger around these prophecies — which is exactly the unease Neo now carries into the elevator.
sc-081: The blind man's knowing nod and the secluded building establish the Oracle's world as one of hidden authority, priming Neo's anxious need to verify what he is walking into.
ev-019: Morpheus's announcement that he is taking Neo to the Oracle sets this journey in motion; this scene is the briefing he gives en route.
sets_up: ev-021: Neo's insistence on whether the Oracle is 'never wrong' and Morpheus's 'guide, not right-or-wrong' framing prepare Neo to receive a prophecy he will have to interpret for himself rather than accept as a verdict — the Oracle's test of his perception.

ev-021: Morpheus's disclosure that the Oracle told him he would find the One grounds the faith that will make him willing to die for Neo, and that will be strained when the Oracle does not confirm Neo as the One.
The 'right and wrong' reframe sets up the later collision between faith and proof that governs the Oracle's apartment and Morpheus's capture.
dramatic_function: To convert Neo's abstract curiosity about the Oracle into a personal, faith-versus-proof tension: it establishes the Oracle as a fallible-sounding guide while revealing that Morpheus's certainty rests entirely on an unfulfilled prophecy, so the audience understands both why Neo must be tested and why Morpheus will stake his life on the outcome.
